Hello there! It's interesting you've noticed that shift in your thinking. This phenomenon is closely related to the concept of cognitive dissonance, a psychological term that describes the mental discomfort experienced by holding two or more contradictory beliefs, values, or ideas at the same time.

In your case, when you're feeling 'opposite' of something good, your mind might cling to that negative feeling because it's trying to maintain internal consistency. This resistance to change is one of the key factors in cognitive dissonance.

As for day-old ideas, we were discussing how our minds tend to cling to initial impressions and resist new information, even when it contradicts our existing beliefs. This reluctance to change can sometimes make us feel 'opposite' to new ideas, as you've experienced. Understanding cognitive dissonance can help us navigate these situations more effectively.
